legal.headline: Balance sheet entries can acknowledge a debt and renew limitation under Section 18, Limitation Act: SC restores money recovery suit
legal.hook: Observing that at the Order VII Rule 11 stage, the amount owed is for trial, the Supreme Court revived the suit rejected by the High Court as time barred
legal.summary: Supreme Court holds that balance sheet entries, read with bank records, can acknowledge liability under Section 18, Limitation Act, and revive a money recovery suit rejected as time-barred. Supreme Court: In an appeal concerning rejection of a money recovery suit as barred by limitation, the three-Judge Bench of Vikram Nath* , Augustine George Masih and Sandeep Mehta, JJ., held that entries in the defendant-Society’s balance sheets, read in the context of the surrounding transactions and bank records, could constitute acknowledgement of liability under Section 18 , Limitation Act, 1963 .
legal.contextNote: The Supreme Court held that entries in a society’s balance sheet, when read alongside bank records, can amount to an acknowledgment of liability under Section 18 of the Limitation Act, 1963, thereby reviving a money recovery suit previously dismissed as time‑barred. The bench (Justices Vikram Nath, Augustine George Masih and Sandeep Mehta) applied this principle to a claim of ₹11,16,000 against Loke Delhi Advertising CGHS Ltd, finding the plaintiff’s claim of ₹11,04,840 (a 9% change) recoverable. No other precedent was cited in the excerpt.

legal.headline: Can the police block a Facebook page through an SP’s intimation to Meta? P&H HC clarifies the authority prescribed under IT Rules, 2021
